- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% relative to prior peak.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overshoots in next 3–5 days; apply downward correction of 3–8% to avoid overreaction.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.33) and price is falling, model frequently underestimates the drop; adjust forecast downward by 1–4% to match sentiment-driven decline.
- Model shows persistent lag in mean reversion: if price is above 30-day moving average, forecast tends to stay above; if below, it lags below — apply 1–3 day lag correction to align with sentiment-driven momentum.
- For 30-day horizon, model underestimates true price volatility in low-sentiment periods; increase forecast variance by 10–20% if sentiment <0.50.
- When sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67), model often averages out extremes; use sentiment-weighted median of recent 5-day prices to anchor forecast.
